title: Draw a Riddle · Teams
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Draw a Riddle · Teams with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose an object with a recognizable function. The lead draws one picture showing what the object does, but not the object itself. The others infer the intended object. Form two teams. Each team has four turns; only the lead’s teammates respond or assist. Each success earns the team one point. The higher team score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Draw a Riddle, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The others infer the intended object.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: The others infer the intended object.
